what_it_does: Running large language models (LLMs — AI text models like chatbots) in a cloud data center alternates between two very different phases: a 'prefill' phase that reads your prompt and does heavy parallel computation, and a 'decode' phase that generates the answer word by word in a less compute-intensive but more power-hungry streaming fashion. These phases happen in milliseconds and have very different heat and power signatures, but cloud power and cooling systems make decisions at much longer timescales, so they are poorly matched. TAPAS is a scheduling system that tracks these millisecond-level power and temperature swings per LLM job and uses model configuration settings — such as how the model is split across chips, its size, and whether numbers are stored in a compressed form (using fewer bits to represent each number, a technique called quantization) — as dials to reduce overheating and power spikes. It also handles the complication that a cloud host runs both its own LLM services (where it has full control) and customer-owned virtual machines (where it has less visibility), applying different strategies for each.
